Echoing @needlestack. Here's an exercise to strengthen the muscles around your knee and improve the elasticity of the tendons:

Stand upright with your feet directly underneath your hips. Lift up the foot from the non injured leg (for these purposes I'll assume that's your left leg raises), bend your other knee slightly, and move your weight to the ball of your planted foot, lifting up your heel off the floor.

Now imagine there is an XY axis under your foot and you are standing at (0,0). Or a cross and you are at the center with lines shooting directly in front, behind, and out pararell to your arms.

Tap your lifted foot at the top of the cross or at (0,10), then the left (-10,0), then behind you (0,-10), then across/in front of your body the right (10,0). Repeat this until you feel your muscles fatigue. That could be 5 sets it could be 30. Then repeat it on the other leg for balance.

I would also do a few sets of this as a warm up before hiking. You should start to feel better in a few weeks of doing this daily!
